A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PENCIL research work. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the main text, equations, all figures and tables, and Appendices A–C, including material shifted between pages.

before.justification: v2 reports original PENCIL benchmark results, heuristic-estimation experiments, ablations, synthetic-graph experiments and computational measurements in the main text and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, synthetic-graph experiments and computational measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same tokenization, Transformer and multiplicative-residual updates, linear link readout and BCE loss. The wider states, identity maps and nonlinear scorer introduced in Appendix B concern theoretical constructions; no corresponding change to the experimental model is reported.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same Planetoid and OGB datasets, heuristic-regression tasks, latent-space graph scenarios and synthetic graphs used for extraction-overhead measurements. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within the benchmark tables, heuristic-regression plots, ablations and computational comparisons. Tables 7–8 retain the same CN, AA and RA comparisons alongside the same learned baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain the original and HeaRT protocols, splits, negative sampling, metrics, model configurations, training budgets and synthetic-data settings. The new theoretical width construction is not reported as an experimental configuration change.

E4.justification: The depth, multiplicative-residual, initialization, multiple-labeled-subgraph, latent-signal and computational-overhead analyses retain the same questions and evidence in Section 5.2 and Appendices C.3–C.7.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random seeds for Planetoid and three for OGB, with unchanged uncertainty-reporting practices. The initialization experiments retain five-run averages, and Table 13 retains timing means and standard deviations over 50 batches.

E6.justification: Matched result tables, plotted results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout both PDFs. For example, Table 1 retains ogbl-ppa Hits@100 of 79.54 ± 0.07 for PENCIL with features and 73.85 ± 0.40 without features.

T1.justification: v3 adds Lemma B.2 and its block-coordinate proof that a residual MPNN of width D=(K+1)d can simulate non-residual iterations. Proofs of Propositions 4.2 and 4.5 replace v2's zero-map Transformer construction with identity maps and this lemma; Corollary 4.3's proof is also revised. v3 additionally specifies loop-free theoretical adjacency, fixed normalized Rademacher vectors and a nonlinear-MLP readout assumption. These substantially revise the mathematical support for central heuristic-expressivity results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about plain Transformers, parameter efficiency, structural-signal recovery and expressivity. Revised supporting proofs do not change the stated main contributions or their scope.

C2.justification: New discussion following Lemma B.2 explains that the enlarged width is sufficient for the proof rather than an inherent model requirement, and describes architectural modifications that could avoid it. Existing empirical interpretations and the limitations in Section 7 and Appendix C remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The sampler, software libraries, frozen input projection, hyperparameter Tables 4–6, GPU information and code-access statement are retained. The new theoretical assumptions are not disclosed as changes to implementation or experimental settings.

R1.justification: Citation changes update metadata for existing works, including Müller et al.'s publication information and the years for Lachi et al. and Yehudai et al. No cited work is substantively added or removed, and research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds Appendix B.2, locally rewrites several proofs, and updates subsection numbering, theorem references and bibliographic metadata. The main narrative and overall document organization are retained.

P2.justification: Appendix displays reflow: Figure 6 and Table 4 become separated across pages, and Table 10 now precedes Figure 7. All ten figures and fourteen tables remain, with unchanged graphical content and table designs; there is no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 improves the theoretical justification by replacing v2's zero-map reduction, which does not preserve message passing in Eq. (3), with an identity-map construction and an explicit residual-simulation lemma. The gain is limited by an unresolved connection to the stated architecture: the revised Proposition 4.5 proof assumes a nonlinear MLP scorer, while Section 3.2 still specifies a linear readout. The revision therefore provides clearer reasoning and assumptions without fully reconciling the theory and model; empirical evidence remains unchanged.
